newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hochtief not interested in pooled Holzmann stake.
newsitem.headline: Hochtief not interested in pooled Holzmann stake.

text.p: German construction group Hochtief AG said on Monday it was no longer interested in pooling resources with Deutsche Bank AG to take a stake in fellow builder Philip Holzmann AG.
In late April, Hochtief and Deutsche requested clearance from the European Commission for joint control of Holzmann.
Under the arrangement, Deutsche and Hochtief were to pool stakes totalling almost 50 percent of Holzmann -- Deutsche with 25.8 percent and Hochtief with 20 percent.
Hochtief has been trying to increase its influence on Holzmann's board for years in an attempt to work more closely on projects outside Germany.
Hochtief also said it would not close the door to buying an additional stake in Holzmann as it had said it would in March.
The builder said it had decided after all against annulling a deal with Commerzbank AG to buy a further 10 percent stake in Holzmann.
In a separate statement, Deutsche Bank said it and Hochtief still wanted to support Holzmann which has racked up losses in the past.
"Both companies remain determined to continue supporting Philipp Holzmann," Deutsche and Hochtief said in a statement.
Deutsche also said that the European Commission planned to send the proposed pooled-asset deal to the German Federal Cartel Office.
German authorities had in March rejected the plans of Deutsche Bank and Hochtief and said they wanted to regain responsibility for the Holzmann case from the European Commission.
